questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (d) है। कथन (d) कट्टर व्यवहारवाद (वाटसन और स्किनर) की मान्यता का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है, जिसे बांडुरा ने अपर्याप्त मानकर खारिज कर दिया था। बांडुरा के सामाजिक अधिगम सिद्धांत के मुख्य स्तंभ हैं: (1) व्यक्ति दूसरों के व्यवहार और उनके परिणामों का अवलोकन करके सीख सकते हैं, (2) अधिगम एक आंतरिक मानसिक प्रक्रिया है, इसलिए व्यवहार में तुरंत बदलाव दिखे बिना भी व्यक्ति बहुत कुछ सीख सकता है (गुप्त अधिगम), और (3) संज्ञान, प्रत्याशाएं और आत्म-नियमन अधिगम में केंद्रीय भूमिका निभाते हैं। यह दावा करना कि समस्त व्यवहार केवल शास्त्रीय व क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन से निर्धारित होता है, सामाजिक अधिगम सिद्धांत के विपरीत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) All behavior is determined solely by classical and operant conditioning.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: and operant conditioning.
Social Learning Theory expands beyond traditional behaviorism by demonstrating that cognitive processing mediates learning and that observation produces learning without immediate behavioral change or direct reinforcement. Attributing all human behavior strictly to classical and operant conditioning ignores cognitive mediation, observational modeling, and self-regulatory mechanisms central to Bandura’s theory.

questions.question_english: Adolescent psychology identifies several key developmental challenges during the transition from childhood to adulthood. Which of the following is considered the primary psychosocial crisis of adolescence according to Erik Erikson’s epigenetic theory?
options_english: Trust vs. Mistrust
Industry vs. Inferiority
Identity vs. Role Confusion
Intimacy vs. Isolation
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is (c) Identity vs. Role Confusion. In Erik Erikson’s eight-stage theory of psychosocial development, the fifth stage (occurring during adolescence, approximately ages 12–18) is characterized by the crisis of Identity versus Role Confusion. Adolescents undergo significant biological, cognitive, and social changes, prompting them to explore personal values, philosophical beliefs, vocational goals, gender identity, and interpersonal roles to forge an integrated, coherent sense of self ('Who am I?'). Successful resolution leads to the virtue of 'Fidelity'. Failure to resolve this crisis results in identity diffusion, occupational indecision, and role confusion.
For reference:
- Trust vs. Mistrust occurs in Infancy (Stage 1)
- Industry vs. Inferiority occurs in School Age (Stage 4)
- Intimacy vs. Isolation occurs in Young Adulthood (Stage 6).
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर (c) पहचान बनाम भूमिका भ्रांति/संभ्रम (Identity vs. Role Confusion) है। एरिक एरिक्सन के मनोसामाजिक विकास के आठ चरणों में, पाँचवाँ चरण किशोरावस्था (लगभग 12 से 18 वर्ष) से संबंधित है। इस चरण का मुख्य विकासात्मक संकट 'पहचान बनाम भूमिका संभ्रम' है। इस अवस्था में किशोर शारीरिक, संज्ञानात्मक और सामाजिक परिवर्तनों से गुजरते हुए अपने व्यक्तिगत मूल्यों, व्यावसायिक आकांक्षाओं और सामाजिक भूमिकाओं का अन्वेषण करते हैं ताकि वे एक सुसंगत पहचान ('मैं कौन हूँ?') का निर्माण कर सकें। इस संकट का सफल समाधान 'निष्ठा' (Fidelity) का सद्गुण विकसित करता है, जबकि विफलता से भूमिका संभ्रम और दिशाहीनता उत्पन्न होती है।
अन्य चरण:
- विश्वास बनाम अविश्वास: शैशवावस्था (चरण 1)
- परिश्रम बनाम हीनता: उत्तर बाल्यावस्था/स्कूली आयु (चरण 4)
- घनिष्ठता बनाम अलगाव: प्रारंभिक वयस्कता (चरण 6)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Identity vs. Role Confusion

Unsuccessful resolution results in role confusion, lack of direction, and identity instability.

questions.question_english: Which of the following is an example of ‘negative reinforcement’ used as an extrinsic motivator in a classroom?

Providing a tangible reward like chocolate for demonstrating good behavior
Detaining a disruptive student during recess for submitting incomplete work

questions.explanation_english: In operant conditioning, negative reinforcement involves strengthening or increasing the future frequency of a desirable behavior by removing, terminating, or avoiding an aversive or unpleasant stimulus upon performance of that behavior. Removing an unwanted homework assignment in response to exceptional classroom conduct illustrates negative reinforcement: an unpleasant task is eliminated to reinforce and increase positive classroom engagement. Option B represents positive reinforcement (presenting a pleasant stimulus). Option C represents punishment/detention (applying an unpleasant consequence to reduce undesirable behavior). Option D represents extinction (withholding reinforcement to diminish an unwanted response).

questions.question_english: Which prominent psychological theorist formulated the 'Hierarchy of Needs', a cornerstone framework in humanistic theories of motivation?
options_english: Abraham Maslow
B.F. Skinner
Lev Vygotsky
Sigmund Freud
questions.explanation_english: Abraham Maslow, a founding pioneer of humanistic psychology, formulated the 'Hierarchy of Needs' in his landmark 1943 paper 'A Theory of Human Motivation'. Maslow conceptualized human needs arranged in a hierarchical pyramid: beginning with lower-order deficiency needs (Physiological, Safety, Belongingness/Love, and Esteem) that must typically be fulfilled before an individual can pursue higher-order growth needs (Cognitive, Aesthetic, and Self-Actualization). In educational settings, Maslow's theory reminds administrators and teachers that students cannot focus on higher-level academic learning if their physiological needs (nutrition) or safety needs are compromised. B.F. Skinner is associated with operant conditioning, Lev Vygotsky with social constructivism, and Sigmund Freud with psychoanalysis.
questions.explanation_hindi: मानवतावादी मनोविज्ञान के प्रमुख प्रवर्तक अब्राहम मास्लो (Abraham Maslow) ने वर्ष 1943 में 'आवश्यकताओं के पदानुक्रम सिद्धांत' (Hierarchy of Needs Theory) का प्रतिपादन किया था। मास्लो ने मानवीय आवश्यकताओं को एक पिरामिड के रूप में व्यवस्थित किया, जिसमें सबसे नीचे अभाव आवश्यकताएं (शारीरिक, सुरक्षा, स्नेह/संबद्धता, और सम्मान) आती हैं तथा शीर्ष पर विकास आवश्यकताएं (ज्ञानार्जन, सौंदर्यबोध और आत्म-साक्षात्कार/सेल्फ-एक्चुअलाइजेशन) स्थित होती हैं। विद्यालयी संदर्भ में यह सिद्धांत रेखांकित करता है कि जब तक बच्चों की मूलभूत शारीरिक और सुरक्षा संबंधी जरूरतें पूरी नहीं होतीं, वे उच्च स्तरीय संज्ञानात्मक अधिगम के लिए अभिप्रेरित नहीं हो सकते। अन्य विकल्प: बी.एफ. स्किनर (क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन), लेव वायगोत्स्की (सामाजिक रचनावाद) तथा सिगमंड फ्रायड (मनोविश्लेषणवाद) से संबंधित हैं।

questions.question_english: Which eminent developmental psychologist conceptualized the “Identity Crisis” as the central psychosocial conflict defining the adolescent stage of human development?
options_english: Jean Piaget
Sigmund Freud
Erik Erikson
Lawrence Kohlberg
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is Option C.
Erik Erikson formulated the Eight Stages of Psychosocial Development, spanning the human lifespan. In his fifth stage—Identity vs. Role Confusion (occurring during adolescence, approximately ages 12–18)—the central developmental crisis is establishing a coherent identity:
- Identity Crisis: Adolescents actively explore different roles, occupational aspirations, personal values, ideological beliefs, and sexual identity to synthesize an integrated sense of self.
- Successful resolution leads to the virtue of Fidelity (faithfulness to one's values and social commitments), whereas failure results in role confusion and identity diffusion.
- In contrast, Jean Piaget focused on cognitive development (formal operational thought), Sigmund Freud formulated psychosexual stages (genital stage in adolescence), and Lawrence Kohlberg developed the theory of moral development stages.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प C है।
एरिक एरिक्सन ने मानव जीवन-विस्तार के मनोसामाजिक विकास के आठ चरण (Eight Stages of Psychosocial Development) प्रतिपादित किए। उनके सिद्धांत का पांचवां चरण—'पहचान बनाम भूमिका भ्रम' (Identity vs. Role Confusion)—किशोरावस्था (लगभग 12 से 18 वर्ष) में घटित होता है:
- पहचान का संकट (Identity Crisis): इस अवस्था में किशोर अपनी सामाजिक पहचान, भविष्य के व्यावसायिक लक्ष्यों, व्यक्तिगत मूल्यों और मान्यताओं की खोज करते हैं ताकि वे यह समझ सकें कि 'मैं कौन हूँ?'
- इस संकट के सफल समाधान से 'निष्ठा' (Fidelity) का गुण विकसित होता है, जबकि असफलता से भूमिका संशय या पहचान का बिखराव (Role Confusion) उत्पन्न होता है।
- अन्य विकल्प: जीन पियाजे ने संज्ञानात्मक विकास का सिद्धांत दिया, सिगमंड फ्रायड ने मनोविश्लेषणात्मक/मनोकामुक सिद्धांत प्रतिपादित किया, तथा लॉरेंस कोहलबर्ग ने नैतिक विकास के चरण प्रस्तुत किए।

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Erik Erikson proposed identity crisis as the central psychosocial conflict of adolescence (Identity vs. Role Confusion), during which individuals explore roles to develop a coherent identity.

questions.question_english: In Abraham Maslow's motivational hierarchy, which of the following is categorized as a 'growth need' (being need or B-need) rather than a 'deficiency need' (D-need)?

The physiological need for food, water, and rest
The need for interpersonal belongingness and love
The need for self-actualization and personal fulfillment
questions.explanation_english: Abraham Maslow bifurcated human motivational drives into two categories: Deficiency Needs (D-needs), which arise from deprivation (Physiological, Safety, Belongingness/Love, and Esteem), and Growth Needs (Being Needs or B-needs), which arise from the intrinsic human desire to realize one's unique potential, expand capabilities, and attain personal self-fulfillment. Self-actualization is the quintessential growth need. Unlike deficiency needs, which dissipate once satisfied, growth needs are self-perpetuating and deepen as they are pursued, driving continuous lifelong learning and personal evolution.
questions.explanation_hindi: मास्लो ने मानवीय आवश्यकताओं को दो व्यापक श्रेणियों में विभाजित किया है: अभाव आवश्यकताएं (Deficiency Needs या D-Needs): ये किसी चीज़ की कमी से उत्पन्न होती हैं और जब पूरी हो जाती हैं, तो इनकी तीव्रता घट जाती है। इनमें शारीरिक आवश्यकताएं (विकल्प B), सुरक्षा (विकल्प A), प्रेम व संबद्धता (विकल्प C), और सम्मान की आवश्यकता शामिल हैं। विकास आवश्यकताएं (Growth Needs या B-Needs): ये किसी कमी से नहीं बल्कि आत्म-विकास, सृजनात्मकता और अपनी पूर्ण क्षमता को साकार करने की आंतरिक चाह से उत्पन्न होती हैं। 'आत्म-साक्षात्कार' (Self-Actualization - विकल्प D) सर्वोच्च विकास आवश्यकता है। यह आवश्यकता पूरी होने पर समाप्त नहीं होती, बल्कि व्यक्ति में निरंतर और अधिक सीखने व विकसित होने की प्रेरणा को जाग्रत रखती है। अतः विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: A Principal observes a class where the teacher gives a sticker to every student who finishes their homework, regardless of the quality of the work. Over time, the quality of homework declines. This is an example of the negative impact of:
options_english: Engagement-contingent rewards
Informational rewards
Verbal praise
Vicarious reinforcement
questions.explanation_english: This scenario demonstrates the negative effects of 'engagement-contingent' (or completion-contingent) rewards. In educational psychology, engagement-contingent rewards are provided simply for engaging in or completing a task, without any standard of quality, depth, or performance. When students realize that merely finishing or handing in an assignment guarantees the tangible incentive (the sticker), their goal orientation shifts toward completing the task as rapidly and effortlessly as possible to collect the payoff. This results in rushed, superficial, and shoddy work. In contrast, informational rewards (Option B) provide diagnostic feedback on competence, and verbal praise (Option C) emphasizes effort rather than transactional tokens.
questions.explanation_hindi: यह परिदृश्य 'संलग्नता-आकस्मिक' (Engagement-contingent) अथवा कार्य-पूर्णता पुरस्कारों के नकारात्मक प्रभाव को दर्शाता है। शैक्षिक मनोविज्ञान में, संलग्नता-आकस्मिक पुरस्कार वे होते हैं जो किसी कार्य को केवल पूरा करने या जमा करने पर दे दिए जाते हैं, चाहे कार्य की गुणवत्ता या सीखने की गहराई कैसी भी हो। जब विद्यार्थियों को यह समझ आ जाता है कि केवल कार्य पूरा दिखाने भर से स्टिकर मिल जाएगा, तो उनका संपूर्ण ध्यान गुणवत्तापूर्ण अधिगम के बजाय कार्य को यथाशीघ्र और न्यूनतम प्रयास में निपटाने पर केंद्रित हो जाता है। इसके फलस्वरूप गृहकार्य की गुणवत्ता तेजी से गिर जाती है। सूचनात्मक पुरस्कार (विकल्प B) और मौखिक प्रशंसा (विकल्प C) गुणवत्ता और प्रयास को प्रोत्साहित करते हैं। अतः विकल्प (A) सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: How can a teacher best help a student shift from an external locus of control toward a more adaptive internal locus of control?
options_english: By assigning grades randomly to demonstrate to students that academic outcomes are completely unpredictable
By linking specific study strategies directly to test results
By consistently attributing poor academic performance to the student’s personal socio-economic background
By significantly lowering academic expectations so that the student easily succeeds on every assignment
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (b) By linking specific study strategies directly to test results. Shifting a student’s locus of control from external to internal requires attribution retraining. When teachers provide explicit, metacognitive feedback that demonstrates how employing particular study techniques (such as distributed practice, summarizing, self-quizzing) and dedicated effort directly produce measurable academic gains, students realize that outcomes are controllable through their own agency. In contrast, random grading (a) breeds learned helplessness, attributing failure to socio-economic background (c) cements an external/uncontrollable locus, and lowering expectations (d) deprives students of authentic mastery experiences.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। विद्यार्थियों में बाह्य नियंत्रण से आंतरिक नियंत्रण की दिशा में बदलाव लाने के लिए 'गुणारोपण पुनर्प्रशिक्षण' (Attribution Retraining) सबसे कारगर तकनीक है। जब शिक्षक विद्यार्थियों को यह स्पष्ट रूप से दिखाते हैं कि कैसे विशिष्ट अध्ययन रणनीतियों (जैसे सक्रिय स्मरण, संक्षेपण, समय प्रबंधन) और लक्षित प्रयासों के प्रयोग से सीधे उनके अंकों में सुधार हुआ है, तो विद्यार्थी यह अनुभव करने लगते हैं कि परिणाम उनके अपने नियंत्रण में हैं। इसके विपरीत, मनमाने ग्रेड देना (a) लाचारी पैदा करता है, सामाजिक पृष्ठभूमि को दोष देना (c) बाह्य निर्भरता बढ़ाता है, और मानकों को गिराना (d) वास्तविक आत्म-प्रभावकारिता का निर्माण नहीं होने देता।

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): It is generally not advisable to offer tangible rewards for reading books to children who already love reading.
Reason (R): Offering rewards for an already intrinsically motivating activity may lead to the overjustification effect, making the child view reading as ‘work’.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). The 'overjustification effect' occurs when an expected external incentive (such as money, prizes, or pizza parties for reading) decreases an individual's intrinsic motivation to perform a task. When children who already love reading receive prizes for reading, they unconsciously shift their cognitive attribution: instead of believing 'I read because I find books fascinating,' they begin to think 'I read because I am earning a prize.' When the external reward is eventually discontinued, their reading frequency often plummets below baseline levels because reading has been redefined in their minds as instrumental labor rather than autonomous leisure.
questions.explanation_hindi: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सटीक व्याख्या करता है। मनोविज्ञान में इसे 'अति-औचित्य प्रभाव' (Overjustification Effect - लेपर, ग्रीन और निस्बेट) कहा जाता है। जब किसी ऐसी गतिविधि के लिए मूर्त बाह्य पुरस्कार (जैसे पैसे, खिलौने या टोकन) पेश किए जाते हैं जिसे बच्चा पहले से ही शौक और आनंद से करता है, तो बच्चा अपने व्यवहार का श्रेय उस बाह्य पुरस्कार को देने लगता है। बच्चा यह सोचने लगता है कि वह पुस्तक केवल इनाम पाने के लिए पढ़ रहा है, जिससे पढ़ने का स्वाभाविक आनंद 'मजदूरी' या 'कार्य' में बदल जाता है। परिणामस्वरूप, पुरस्कार बंद होते ही बच्चे का पढ़ना भी बंद हो जाता है। अतः विकल्प (A) सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

When rewards are introduced, children reattribute their reading behavior to earning prizes rather than personal enjoyment, viewing reading as work. This psychological shift directly explains why tangible rewards can undermine existing intrinsic motivation.

questions.question_english: Which sequence correctly represents the cyclical stages of the motivational cycle in psychological theory?
options_english: Drive, Need, Incentive, Reward
Need, Drive, Arousal, Goal-directed behaviour, Achievement, Drive reduction
Incentive, Goal-directed behaviour, Need, Drive reduction
Arousal, Reward, Need, Drive
questions.explanation_english: The standard motivational cycle in psychological theory follows a defined homeostatic sequence: (1) Need: a state of biological or psychological deprivation, which produces (2) Drive: an internal state of physiological tension, triggering (3) Arousal: an energetic state prompting action, which leads to (4) Goal-directed behaviour: purposeful action oriented toward satisfying the need, culminating in (5) Achievement: reaching the goal or attaining the incentive, and finally resulting in (6) Drive reduction: relief of tension and restoration of internal equilibrium (homeostasis). Once reduced, new needs arise, continuing the cycle.
questions.explanation_hindi: मनोविज्ञान में अभिप्रेरणा चक्र (Motivational Cycle) छह क्रमिक और चक्रीय चरणों का अनुसरण करता है: (1) आवश्यकता (Need - किसी जैविक या मनोवैज्ञानिक अभाव की स्थिति), जो जन्म देती है (2) प्रणोद (Drive - अंतर्नोद या आंतरिक तनाव) को, जिससे (3) उत्तेजना (Arousal) उत्पन्न होती है, यह उत्तेजना प्राणी को (4) लक्ष्य-निर्देशित व्यवहार (Goal-directed behaviour) करने के लिए प्रेरित करती है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप (5) उपलब्धि (Achievement - लक्ष्य की प्राप्ति) होती है, और अंततः (6) प्रणोद न्यूनता (Drive reduction - तनाव में कमी तथा आंतरिक संतुलन की बहाली) होती है। इसके पश्चात नई आवश्यकता के साथ यह चक्र पुनः आरंभ हो जाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Need, Drive, Arousal, Goal-directed behaviour, Achievement, Drive reduction

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: behaviour, Achievement, Drive reduction The motivational cycle follows a structured psychological sequence beginning with an unsatisfied need that creates an internal drive. This drive generates psychological arousal, prompting individuals to engage in goal-directed behavior. Successfully attaining the desired goal results in achievement, which subsequently leads to drive reduction and restores emotional and physiological equilibrium within the learner.

questions.question_english: A School Principal conducting a pedagogical workshop on 'Teacher Expectations' advises the faculty to practice “equity in wait time.” In classroom practice, this implies that teachers should:
options_english: Provide all students with equal, adequate thinking time before requiring them to respond
Wait significantly longer only for high-achieving students to formulate complex, comprehensive answers
Require struggling learners to stand outside the classroom if they cannot recall an answer quickly
Continuously fire rapid recall questions to maintain a fast-paced instructional tempo
questions.explanation_english: Mary Budd Rowe's pioneering research on classroom discourse identified 'Wait Time'—the pause between a teacher asking a question and a student responding (Wait Time 1), as well as the pause after a student speaks before the teacher responds (Wait Time 2). Extending wait time to at least 3 to 5 seconds significantly enhances student verbal fluency, higher-order reasoning, and participation. 'Equity in wait time' specifically mandates that teachers do not rush struggling or hesitant learners while patiently indulging perceived high-achievers. By granting equal, unhurried processing time to all learners regardless of perceived capability, teachers tangibly communicate equal academic respect and high intellectual expectations.
questions.explanation_hindi: मैरी बड रोवे (Mary Budd Rowe) के शोध के अनुसार, 'प्रतीक्षा समय' (Wait Time) शिक्षक द्वारा प्रश्न पूछे जाने और छात्र द्वारा उत्तर दिए जाने के बीच का चिंतन विराम होता है। जब इस विराम को 3 से 5 सेकंड तक बढ़ाया जाता है, तो छात्रों के संज्ञानात्मक प्रसंस्करण, तार्किक चिंतन और भागीदारी में अभूतपूर्व वृद्धि होती है। 'प्रतीक्षा समय में समानता' (Equity in wait time) का सीधा अर्थ है कि शिक्षक प्रत्येक विद्यार्थी को—चाहे वह मेधावी हो या सीखने में धीमा—उत्तर तैयार करने के लिए समान और गरिमापूर्ण सोचने का अवसर दें। प्रायः शिक्षक कमजोर समझे जाने वाले छात्रों को तुरंत टोक देते हैं या दूसरे छात्र से पूछ लेते हैं, जिससे उनकी आत्म-प्रभावकारिता घटती है। समान प्रतीक्षा समय देना सभी छात्रों की बौद्धिक क्षमता में समान विश्वास व्यक्त करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Give all students equal, adequate time to think before responding

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Equity in wait time requires teachers to provide every student with adequate thinking time after asking a question. Extending wait time allows all learners, regardless of perceived confidence or skill level, to process information and formulate responses, signaling equal confidence in their intellectual abilities.

options_hindi: हॉथोर्न प्रभाव (The Hawthorne Effect)
ज़िगारनिक प्रभाव (The Zeigarnik Effect)
प्रीमैक सिद्धांत (The Premack Principle)
पिग्मेलियन प्रभाव (The Pygmalion Effect)

questions.question_english: A Principal notes that a teacher frequently uses the statement: “If you complete this worksheet, you can have 10 minutes of free time.” This technique relies on:
options_english: The Hawthorne Effect
The Zeigarnik Effect
The Premack Principle
The Pygmalion Effect
questions.explanation_english: The teacher's technique is a direct application of the Premack Principle (commonly known as 'Grandma's Rule'), formulated by David Premack. This behavioral principle states that a high-probability or highly preferred behavior (such as enjoying unstructured free time or playing) can serve as an effective positive reinforcer for a low-probability or less preferred behavior (such as completing an academic worksheet). Option A (Hawthorne Effect) refers to subjects modifying behavior due to awareness of being observed. Option B (Zeigarnik Effect) refers to the tendency to remember interrupted or uncompleted tasks better than completed ones. Option D (Pygmalion Effect) refers to the phenomenon where higher teacher expectations lead to enhanced student achievement.
questions.explanation_hindi: यह तकनीक डेविड प्रीमैक द्वारा प्रतिपादित 'प्रीमैक सिद्धांत' (Premack Principle - जिसे आम बोलचाल में 'दादी का नियम' भी कहा जाता है) पर आधारित है। यह सिद्धांत बताता है कि किसी उच्च-संभाव्यता वाले या अत्यधिक पसंदीदा व्यवहार (जैसे स्वतंत्र खाली समय या खेलना) का उपयोग किसी कम पसंदीदा व्यवहार (जैसे शैक्षणिक वर्कशीट पूरा करना) को सुदृढ़ करने के लिए किया जा सकता है। विकल्प A (हॉथोर्न प्रभाव) अवलोकन किए जाने के अहसास से व्यवहार में आने वाले सुधार को दर्शाता है। विकल्प B (ज़िगारनिक प्रभाव) अधूरे कार्यों को पूरे कार्यों की तुलना में अधिक याद रखने से संबंधित है। विकल्प D (पिग्मेलियन प्रभाव) शिक्षक की उच्च अपेक्षाओं के फलस्वरूप छात्र प्रदर्शन में होने वाली वृद्धि को संदर्भित करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) The Premack Principle

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Premack Principle states that a high- probability or highly preferred activity can serve as an effective reinforcer for a low-probability or less preferred activity. By offering free time as a reward contingent upon completing a required academic worksheet, the teacher leverages a desirable activity to motivate engagement in a less appealing task.

questions.question_english: In behavioral management and Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), the ‘Antecedent-Behavior-Consequence’ (ABC) framework is extensively utilized. What does the term ‘Antecedent’ denote?
options_english: The formal disciplinary sanction or punishment administered after an infraction occurs
The underlying biological or genetic predisposition governing a student’s temperament
The environmental trigger or stimulus immediately preceding the occurrence of the behavior
The cumulative longitudinal record of a student’s past academic achievement
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is Option C.
The ABC model of functional behavior assessment (derived from B.F. Skinner's operant conditioning paradigm) breaks down behavioral episodes into three chronological components:
1. Antecedent (A): The specific environmental condition, event, instructional cue, or stimulus that immediately precedes the target behavior and triggers or sets the occasion for it (e.g., being handed a difficult worksheet, a peer whisper, or a transition between activities).
2. Behavior (B): The observable, measurable action or response emitted by the student (e.g., throwing a pencil, yelling, or raising a hand).
3. Consequence (C): The immediate environmental outcome or reaction following the behavior that maintains, reinforces, or discourages its future repetition (e.g., being removed from the class, receiving teacher attention, or earning a token).
Option A describes a consequence, Option B relates to biological etiology, and Option D is background academic history.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प C है।
कार्यात्मक व्यवहार मूल्यांकन (FBA) और अनुप्रयुक्त व्यवहार विश्लेषण (ABA) का ABC मॉडल किसी भी व्यवहार को तीन क्रमिक घटकों में विश्लेषित करता है:
1. पूर्ववृत्त (Antecedent - A): वह विशिष्ट पर्यावरणीय परिस्थिति, घटना, निर्देश या उद्दीपक जो किसी व्यवहार के घटित होने से ठीक पहले उपस्थित होता है और उस व्यवहार को उत्प्रेरित (trigger) करता है (जैसे- कोई कठिन कार्य मिलना, सहपाठी की टिप्पणी, या गतिविधियों में बदलाव)।
2. व्यवहार (Behavior - B): विद्यार्थी द्वारा की गई प्रत्यक्ष, मापने योग्य और अवलोकनीय क्रिया या प्रतिक्रिया (जैसे- मेज पर सिर पटकना, चिल्लाना, या शांत होकर हाथ उठाना)।
3. परिणाम (Consequence - C): व्यवहार के ठीक बाद घटित होने वाली पर्यावरणीय प्रतिक्रिया या परिणाम, जो यह निर्धारित करता है कि वह व्यवहार भविष्य में पुनः दोहराया जाएगा या नहीं (जैसे- शिक्षक का ध्यान आकर्षित होना या कक्षा से बाहर भेजा जाना)।
विकल्प A परिणाम (Consequence) को दर्शाता है, विकल्प B जैविक कारणों से संबंधित है, और विकल्प D शैक्षणिक इतिहास है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) The trigger immediately preceding the behavior

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: behavior In behavioral analysis, the Antecedent refers to the stimulus, event, or environmental trigger occurring immediately before a behavior, setting the stage for its occurrence and providing key insight for behavior management.

questions.question_english: Bernard Weiner’s Attribution Theory fundamentally focuses on:
options_english: How individuals explain event causes and how it affects behavior
The sequential physiological and biological stages involved in cognitive development
The psychometric measurement and evaluation of individual intelligence quotients
The formal administrative organizational structure governing school system operations
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (a) How individuals explain event causes and how it affects behavior. Bernard Weiner’s Attribution Theory provides a cognitive framework explaining how individuals explain the causes of their successes and failures. Weiner argued that when students experience an academic outcome, they instinctively ask 'Why did this happen?' (e.g., Was it my effort, my ability, task difficulty, or luck?). The cognitive explanation (attribution) they arrive at determines their subsequent emotional reactions (pride, shame, guilt, hope), their future expectations of success, and their willingness to persist in learning tasks.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। बर्नार्ड वीनर का कारण-गुणारोपण सिद्धांत (Attribution Theory) यह समझने पर केंद्रित है कि शिक्षार्थी अपनी सफलताओं और असफलताओं के कारणों की व्याख्या (गुणारोपण) किस प्रकार करते हैं। किसी परीक्षा या कार्य के परिणाम के बाद विद्यार्थी स्वयं से यह प्रश्न पूछते हैं कि वे सफल या असफल क्यों हुए—क्या इसका कारण उनका अपना प्रयास था, उनकी जन्मजात क्षमता थी, प्रश्नपत्र की कठिनाई थी या भाग्य? यह संज्ञानात्मक कारण-निर्धारण उनके भावी संवेगों (गर्व, लज्जा, निराशा), सफलता की प्रत्याशा और आगे की मेहनत व व्यवहार को गहराई से निर्धारित करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) How individuals explain event causes and how it affects behavior

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: how it affects behavior
Bernard Weiner’s Attribution Theory examines how individuals interpret the causes of successes and failures, and how these cognitive causal attributions influence subsequent emotional reactions, expectations, and achievement behaviors. Understanding causal interpretations helps educators reshape student attributions toward controllable factors, fostering academic resilience and self-direction.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements about managing classroom anxiety:
I. High-stakes testing generally decreases anxiety because students know exactly what is expected.
II. Teaching students specific test-taking strategies can reduce test anxiety.
III. Allowing students to express their anxieties (e.g., through writing) before a test can improve performance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Managing classroom anxiety requires research-backed interventions: Statement I is incorrect: High-stakes testing dramatically elevates evaluation threat and anxiety, inducing debilitating worry that impairs working memory performance. Statement II is correct: Equipping students with procedural test-taking strategies (such as systematic pacing, active question deconstruction, and self-monitoring) bolsters perceived competence and mitigates cognitive test anxiety. Statement III is correct: Empirical studies (such as research by Ramirez & Beilock, 2011) demonstrate that expressive writing for 10 minutes prior to an exam allows students to offload intrusive worries from working memory, unburdening cognitive resources and substantially enhancing academic performance. Therefore, statements II and III are correct.

Assertion (A): Establishing a set of collaboratively developed classroom rules at the beginning of the year decreases behavioral issues.

questions.explanation_english: In effective classroom management and Self-Determination Theory (Deci & Ryan), student participation in democratic norm-setting satisfies their fundamental psychological need for autonomy. When rules are imposed unilaterally through authoritarian decree, students perceive them as external constraints, often prompting compliance motivated by fear or triggering passive-aggressive resistance. In contrast, co-constructing classroom expectations cultivates psychological ownership and shifts motivation along the organismic integration continuum toward identified and integrated regulation. Students perceive the norms as meaningful guidelines for a respectful community, leading to voluntary self-regulation and significantly fewer disruptive infractions. Therefore, R directly explains A.

A Principal notices that a teacher maintains an intensely authoritarian classroom climate—rigidly dictating all procedures, exercising punitive control, and severely criticizing errors. While the students are outwardly compliant and silent, they exhibit zero enthusiasm or initiative.

Cultivation of high individual autonomy and divergent creative problem-solving

questions.explanation_english: Applying Diana Baumrind's parenting typologies to classroom environments, an 'authoritarian' climate is characterized by high control and low responsiveness. I. Mastery Goal - Focused on learning, understanding, and self-improvement

questions.explanation_english:
All three pairs are accurately matched according to modern Achievement Goal Theory (Elliot & McGregor; Dweck):
1. Mastery Goals (Pair I): Learners focus on mastering task content, acquiring new knowledge, and judging success against self-referenced standards of progress and effort.
2. Performance-Approach Goals (Pair II): Learners focus on normative standards—aiming to attain superior grades, defeat peers, and attain social validation of their high intelligence.
3. Performance-Avoidance Goals (Pair III): Learners are driven by fear of failure and negative evaluation, focusing on escaping looking foolish, stupid, or inadequate in the eyes of teachers and peers. This orientation is consistently linked to debilitating anxiety and academic self-handicapping.
Therefore, all three pairs (I, II, and III) are correctly matched.

questions.question_english: During the adolescent stage of human development, the psychological phenomenon wherein a teenager persistently feels that they are being closely observed, scrutinized, and evaluated by others is referred to as:
options_english: The personal fable
The imaginary audience
Identity foreclosure
Cognitive dissonance
questions.explanation_english: David Elkind identified the 'Imaginary Audience' as a prominent feature of adolescent egocentrism. During this stage of cognitive and psychosocial transition, adolescents become intensely self-reflective and mistakenly assume that others are as preoccupied with their appearance, behaviors, and flaws as they are with themselves. They construct an internal mental belief that they are constantly 'on stage' before an imaginary audience that continuously monitors, scrutinizes, and evaluates them. This cognitive phenomenon leads to heightened self-consciousness, hypersensitivity to peer judgment, and acute concern regarding social presentation. In contrast, the 'Personal Fable' refers to the belief in one's personal uniqueness and invulnerability; 'Identity Foreclosure' is commitment without exploration; and 'Cognitive Dissonance' describes discomfort from holding conflicting cognitions.
questions.explanation_hindi: डेविड एलकाइंड (David Elkind) ने किशोरावस्था के अहंकेंद्रवाद (Adolescent Egocentrism) के एक प्रमुख घटक के रूप में 'काल्पनिक दर्शक' (Imaginary Audience) की अवधारणा प्रतिपादित की। इस विकासात्मक चरण में, किशोरों में आत्म-जागरूकता अत्यधिक बढ़ जाती है और वे यह मान बैठते हैं कि जिस प्रकार वे स्वयं के प्रति अत्यधिक सचेत हैं, उसी प्रकार आसपास के अन्य सभी लोग भी निरंतर केवल उन्हीं के रूप-रंग, व्यवहार और गतिविधियों को देख रहे हैं तथा उनका मूल्यांकन कर रहे हैं। इस काल्पनिक दर्शक की भावना के कारण किशोरों में अत्यधिक आत्म-सचेतता (self-consciousness), सामाजिक छवि के प्रति चिंता और साथियों की राय को लेकर तीव्र संवेदनशीलता उत्पन्न होती है। इसके विपरीत, 'व्यक्तिगत मिथक' (Personal Fable) अपनी भावनाओं को सर्वथा अद्वितीय और स्वयं को अभेद्य समझने की प्रवृत्ति है; 'पहचान पूर्वबंध' बिना किसी अन्वेषण के पहचान तय कर लेना है; तथा 'संज्ञानात्मक विसंगति' परस्पर विरोधी विचारों के कारण होने वाली मानसिक असहजता है। अतः सही उत्तर (B) है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The imaginary audience

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: David Elkind identified the imaginary audience as an aspect of adolescent egocentrism wherein teenagers construct a belief that they are constantly the center of attention. They imagine that peers and adults are continuously observing, scrutinizing, and evaluating their appearance, behavior, and performance, leading to heightened self-consciousness.
